text:
After 2 years living in BKK, this was my first ever dentist visit. I decided to go to All About Teeth, because the service & the prices seem acceptable to me. The booking process was smooth and easy. They responded my chat fast with useful information too.

Upon arrival, they sent me my appointment card, and I only had to wait for a bit until I received the treatment.

I did dental fillings and scaling treatment. The dentist is super duper friendly, she speaks fluent English and I feel so comfortable because she made sure all procedures were done well. Another plus point is that they DON’T try to sell anything, instead, they only recommend and advise what’s best according to your teeth conditions. The choice is still yours. So no need to feel bad 😆

After the treatment is done, I had a little chat with the dentist and again, she gave me some advice and recommendations for other treatments I might consider to do in the future to make my teeth better.

I would give the service a solid 10/10. For sure, I would visit this clinic again if (hopefully not though🤣) have another tooth problem 5555.

But if you’re looking for a dental clinic, do pay All About Teeth Clinic a visit!

text:
I would just like to state what exactly happened to me in this clinic.

Having recently arrived in Bangkok, I went to a so-called dentist in this clinic, because it was conveniently located in the very same building complex that I had rented a holiday condo.

First and foremost, she charged me the maximum of the cleaning price range, even though I go for scaling every 6 months back in the US, so my teeth are generally not dirty at all.

Also, she did a sloppy job; quick and careless. So, I paid the highest rate (Why not? All foreign tourists must be rich) for a sloppy job.

Furthermore, even though I did not ask for a checkup, she offered to look around. She then said: "Everything looks good. There are no cavities. All is OK."

When I paid and got this piece of paper, I noticed that there was one word written on it in front of "diagnosed with." I looked it up online and realized that it is the name of a gum disease. So, she wrote down that I had some difficult-to-pronounce gum disease, but forgot to even mention it and tell me what it was or how I could manage it. She did not even revise her statement that everything seemed fine.

About a week after that, I broke a tooth, but this time I went to a different dentist that was recommended to me by the estate agent who had found me the holiday condo. This dentist looked at my teeth and said: "I can fix your broken tooth now, but while we are at it, I suggest we also fix your three little cavities before they get worse." And he showed me, of course. I could clearly see in his tiny mirror where the cavities were. And he told me that I had no gum disease.

So, to summarize, her diagnostic prowess was second to none, she slapped a fancy-sounding (but non-existent) gum disease name on my bill and conveniently forget to explain what it was or how to manage it, and indeed she charged me the maximum amount for a quick and sloppy cleaning procedure.

Her name on the bill was prefixed with "Dr.", so she was supposedly a doctor/dentist, not a hygienist.

This was just my experience at this clinic.
